headline: Spain Tests First Open-Sea Solar Farm Off Valencia
meta_description: Spain is testing its first offshore solar installation with two steel catamarans carrying 1,200 panels, capable of powering 500 homes.
summary_short: Spain launches its first open-sea solar farm near Valencia, using floating catamarans to harness ocean energy for coastal communities.
body:
Spain is testing its first open-sea solar farm, with two 220-ton steel catamarans carrying 1,200 solar panels off the coast of Valencia. The 1 MW project represents a significant step in maritime renewable energy, designed to generate enough electricity to power around 500 homes.

The floating installation demonstrates a novel approach to solar generation—moving the technology from rooftops and land into open water, where wind and weather exposure present both challenges and opportunities. The two massive steel vessels serve as stable platforms for the panels, engineered to withstand ocean conditions while capturing sunlight across the Mediterranean.

If successful, this pilot project could open new possibilities for coastal regions seeking to expand renewable energy capacity without competing for limited land space. Spain's venture into floating solar technology signals growing innovation in how nations are reimagining where clean energy can be harvested.
quick_facts: Two 220-ton steel catamarans carrying 1,200 solar panels
Located off the coast of Valencia, Spain
First open-sea solar farm tested in Spain
